title: Bananaland University
author: Josh Brake
summary: Brake uses the Savannah Bananas — a novelty baseball entertainment company that turned stagnant traditions into a 102,000-person sellout at Kyle Field — as an inspiration for reimagining higher education in the age of AI. The key move the Bananas made was to keep the core structure of baseball while ruthlessly targeting the parts that weren't working and replacing them with elements that create genuine human connection and shared experience. Brake argues higher education faces the same challenge: as AI threatens to make content delivery frictionless and personalized, the distinctive value of the residential college experience is precisely what AI cannot replicate — embodied presence, shared endeavor, and the formational power of community. He proposes shifting the university's mission frame from job preparation to character development, from economic utility to vocation, and from career credentialing to the kind of meaning-making that only happens in physical proximity with other humans. The piece is an accessible provocation rather than a policy prescription, but makes a compelling case that the AI moment is an opportunity for bold curricular and structural reimagination, not a threat to be defended against.
points: The Bananas' playbook applied to higher ed is not about entertainment but about ruthless focus on what creates genuine human formation — the university's competitive advantage in an AI world is precisely what AI cannot replicate: embodied presence and shared meaning-making.

As AI makes content delivery frictionless and personalized, the distinctively human elements of college — physical community, proximity, shared struggle, mentorship — become more rather than less valuable, but only if institutions build deliberately around them.

The mission reframe from job preparation to vocation, from career credentialing to character development, is both the honest argument for residential education and the path to institutional differentiation in an AI-saturated market.

AI is accelerating a crisis that was already present in higher education, but it also creates an opening: 'There has never been a better time to throw out your traditional grading scheme' or restructure the syllabus around character development and leadership formation.

The deepest human desire the Bananas satisfy — to be physically in the presence of other living, breathing human beings — is a desire that AI will intensify rather than diminish, and universities that build around it will thrive.
quotes: I want this for my grandkids. I want to create something that we love. It's all about chasing moments, guys. You bring people together. There's nothing like it. When you see after a game, thousands of people singing Stand By Me, they feel like they're a part of something.

Cole is ruthless about finding things that aren't working and trying out new things to replace them. Why not think about what we could do to restructure our institutions by taking the core values and principles that we believe in, but don't hold so tightly to the playbook of how everything has been done?

How would we change the shape of the college and university if we shifted our goal from job to vocation, from career preparation to character development, from creating students with economic utility to forming students who understand their place in the world more deeply?

There is an opportunity hiding in plain sight. A counter-narrative that it would be wise for us to attend to. It's the realization that in a world where more and more of our experiences are mediated by digital technology, humans will increasingly crave authentic connection with other embodied human beings.

At its best, the college and university creates a certain environment where shared endeavors can be pursued. Where space, time, and attention can be turned toward ideas and the kind of dialogue and shared meaning-making that is not easily created elsewhere.
Even with our near zero-latency Zoom calls, this kind of experience cannot be replicated outside of a physical, embodied experience.

There is a market for bringing people together, a market that satisfies a deep human desire and need that is only going to grow in the coming years: the desire to be physically in the presence of other living, breathing human beings.
